A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReGap/ReMiss study. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete; renamed, reordered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReMiss attack results, closed-source transfer experiments, backdoor reward analyses and appendix evaluations, including Table 1 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds HarmBench transfer, additional target models, safeguard and readability evaluations, and ROC analysis.

M1.justification: The weighted ReGap objective, perplexity regularization, stochastic beam search, replay-buffer generator training and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A's algorithms are reordered and renumbered without changing their steps. Revised coefficient values are experimental settings.

E1.justification: V3 adds HarmBench's 320 prompts as an out-of-distribution transfer test beyond the retained AdvBench and backdoor evaluations. It also adds a defended-target scenario where LlamaGuard filters incoming prompts; v1 used LlamaGuard as an evaluator.

E2.justification: Matched Table 1 comparisons retain AdvPrompter, AutoDAN and GCG. Transfer and robustness comparisons retain AdvPrompter, while target-loss and small/no-reference comparisons already exist in v1. The added evaluations introduce no new competing attack method.

E3.justification: V3 adds Llama3.1-8b-instruct and GPT-4o target settings, GPT-4 success/readability scoring and new robustness protocols. The proxy analysis now includes AdvPrompter-generated attacks, and backdoor evaluation switches from reward accuracy to misspecification rate. Reported defaults change from lambda=2, alpha=100 to lambda=1, alpha=50, with Llama2's alpha changing from 150 to 75 (v1 Appendix B.5; v3 C.6). These disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds suffix-length sensitivity, LlamaGuard defense testing, GPT-4 readability and evaluator checks, out-of-distribution transfer analysis, and ROC validation of ReGap (Figures 5–7 and 10; Table 5). The system-prompt and reference-model ablations and appendix attack examples already exist in v1.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix B.5 and v3 Appendix C.6 both explicitly report a single training run. Neither version supplies repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests; ASR@10 measures attack attempts rather than independent training runs.

E6.justification: All 16 original Table 1 result rows are unchanged. V3 adds Llama3.1 results (test ASR@10: 40.4% versus AdvPrompter's 27.9%), HarmBench/GPT-4o results, readability and safeguard scores, and proxy AUROCs of 0.97 versus 0.82. V1 Table 9's aggregate Llama2 LlamaGuard scores are no longer tabulated. V3 Section 5.2 claims a 7-fold GPT-4 advantage using 3.1%, but Figure 5 retains the earlier 22.1% versus 6.7% comparison.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the formal backdoor diagnostic from the fraction of positive gaps, RewardAcc, to the fraction of negative gaps, MR; the displayed heatmap values complement the earlier accuracies. The implicit-reward derivation and ReGap mathematics remain unchanged, the loss decomposition is relocated, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the transferability claim to GPT-4o and HarmBench out-of-distribution tasks. Closed-source transfer was already reported in v1. The central reward-misspecification thesis, ReGap/ReMiss contributions, AdvBench superiority and readability claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of suffix-length, readability and safeguard trade-offs, but removes v1's substantive limitations concerning practical reference-model availability and computationally intensive search. The central mechanism and regularization explanations remain, with existing discussion consolidated in Appendix B.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-repository link, GPT-4/4o model identifiers and scoring details, and disclosures about baseline universal-suffix optimization and matched suffix lengths. It revises default loss weights. Existing beam-search, LoRA, training-budget, hardware and runtime information is retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for Llama 3, HarmBench, the Trojan Detection Challenge, reward-model distribution shift and readability evaluation. The related-work taxonomy and positioning against target-loss optimization remain substantially unchanged; bibliographic updates to existing works do not constitute new positioning.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: transferability moves into main results, settings and robustness analyses precede mechanism analysis, and the reference-model ablation joins that analysis. Appendices are reordered, objective explanations redistributed, and the abstract expanded. The limitations and ethical-considerations sections are removed.

P2.justification: V3 adds a conceptual diagram and ROC plot, redraws the overview, and converts transfer, system-prompt and evaluator tables into broader figure panels. It consolidates robustness displays, expands the main-text example table using existing appendix examples, and reorganizes algorithm/table layouts. Figure 7 introduces reversed ASR@1/ASR@10 legend labels.

improvement.justification: The added HarmBench, safeguard, GPT-4 evaluation/readability and ROC tests strengthen empirical support beyond v1, while the code link improves reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by deleted practical limitations and new reporting errors: Section 5.2's unsupported 7-fold GPT-4 comparison and Figure 7's reversed ASR labels. The net improvement is therefore limited.
